obligations.title: Stopped value representative
obligations.source_ref: The proof says T is finite almost surely under the stated alternatives, so X_T is well-defined almost surely.
obligations.notes: The canonical real representative uses the textbook stopped value on finite T and an irrelevant fallback only on T = infinity. The old arbitrary-XT agreement interface remains for compatibility, but the canonical theorem constructs the representative internally.
obligations.expected_theorem_signature: A theorem-level representative/agreement bridge proving that the canonical real stopped value agrees with X n on finite events T = n.
obligations.proof_contract_notes: Finite-event agreement is proved locally; the canonical theorem guards the infinite fallback by finite-a.s. case assumptions.

obligations.title: Finite stopped expectations are constant
obligations.source_ref: From Theorem 13.17, E[X^T_n] = E[X_0] for all n.
obligations.notes: The stopped-process integrability and adaptedness facts are now proved inside thm_13_17, so thm_13_18 only imports the finite stopped-expectation identity.
obligations.expected_theorem_signature: def_13_7 P F_n X -> def_13_8 F_n T -> sigma-finiteness -> forall n, integral (def_13_9_stoppedProcess X T n) dP = integral (X 0) dP
obligations.proof_contract_notes: The finite stopped-expectation identity is imported from current passing thm_13_17 and used internally in the parent theorem.

obligations.title: Case (i): bounded stopping time
obligations.source_ref: If T is bounded by C almost surely, the stopped value equals the stopped process at C almost surely, so E[X_T] = E[X^T_C] = E[X_0].
obligations.notes: The bounded case is now proved from the source assumptions T <= C a.s. and stopped-value agreement: these imply XT = X^T_C a.e., hence the integrals agree, and Theorem 13.17 supplies E[X^T_C]=E[X_0].
obligations.expected_theorem_signature: T <= C a.s. and stopped-value agreement imply integral XT dP = integral (X 0) dP using the finite stopped-expectation theorem.
obligations.proof_contract_notes: The equality with the stopped process is derived from the bounded stopping-time source hypothesis.

obligations.title: Case (ii): bounded martingale and dominated convergence
obligations.source_ref: If T is finite almost surely and |X_n| <= K, then X^T_n -> X_T and dominated convergence gives lim E[X^T_n] = E[X_T].
obligations.notes: The stopped-value representative is no longer debt in the canonical route. The remaining support is the DCT conclusion exposed as thm_13_18_stoppedIntegralLimit.

source_output_alignment.next_action: Use the existing theorem part, then replace the remaining support interface with source-aligned local lemmas.

obligations.expected_theorem_signature: Finite T a.s., stopped-value agreement, stopped-process measurability, and the source uniform bound |X_n| <= K imply the stopped-integral limit and then integral XT dP = integral X0 dP using finite stopped expectations.
obligations.proof_contract_notes: The stopped-process bound is derived from the source uniform bound. The retained Integrable constant condition is the formal DCT dominator side condition, not relocation of the stopped-process bound.

obligations.title: Case (iii): integrable T and bounded increments
obligations.source_ref: The telescoping estimate |X^T_n| <= |X_0| + cT gives an integrable dominating function, so dominated convergence again gives lim E[X^T_n] = E[X_T].
obligations.notes: This names the textbook telescoping/DCT obligation explicitly instead of replacing it with the final optional-stopping equality. The canonical route no longer treats the stopped-value representative as debt.

source_output_alignment.next_action: Use the existing theorem part, then replace the remaining support interface with source-aligned local lemmas.

obligations.expected_theorem_signature: Integrable finite representative of T and bounded increments imply an integrable domination bound, then DCT and finite stopped expectations imply the final equality.
obligations.proof_contract_notes: The telescoping dominator is proved and does not remain open proof debt.

obligations.title: Assemble the Martingale Stopping Theorem
obligations.source_ref: In all three cases, combine the finite stopped expectation identity from Theorem 13.17 with the corresponding identification of E[X_T].
obligations.notes: The final theorem consumes the disjunction of the three source cases; the canonical theorem constructs the stopped-value representative internally. Cases (ii) and (iii) still expose DCT support.
obligations.expected_theorem_signature: Given martingale, stopping time, formal sigma-finiteness context, and one of the three source alternatives, prove integral X_T dP = integral X_0 dP.
obligations.proof_contract_notes: The parent theorem reassembles the three source routes without inheriting the old case(ii) stopped-process-bound public premise.
